leftEvidence.role: The cross in letters and later memory
leftEvidence.title: Christ suffers once, the righteous for the unrighteous

points.label: Action and sequence
points.left: Peter says Christ suffered once for sins to bring people to God, was put to death in flesh and made alive in spirit, and continues through proclamation, baptism, and exaltation.
points.right: Weak, ungodly, sinners, and enemies describe the people for whom Christ dies.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The passage materially bears on the Crucifixion while leaving part of its motive, mechanism, or later significance unstated.
points.right: The passage compares a rare human death with Christ’s death while refusing to describe its recipients as deserving.

payload.posture: The passages independently state Christ’s death for others and name different outcomes.

rightEvidence.role: The cross in letters and later memory
rightEvidence.title: Christ dies for the ungodly while they are enemies

payload.tension: Peter moves through righteous and unrighteous, bringing to God, death and life, spirits, baptism, resurrection, and authority; Romans moves through weakness, enemies, blood, rescue, and reconciliation.
payload.title: Once for sins / death for enemies
